mainTopic: When does a גוי acquire wine bought from a Jew, and does משיכה acquire in a deal with a גוי?
overview: The amud continues the גמרא's look at רב's warning that a Jew should take the money before measuring wine for a גוי. The גמרא asks why the money would be forbidden if the גוי acquires the wine before his touch makes it יין נסך. Step by step it narrows רב's case. First it is the גוי's vessel, then a vessel on the ground, and finally a jug with leftover wine on its rim, which forbids each drop at once. It then explains that this fits רב's own view, since he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for barrel among barrels, not wine mixed into wine. Next the גמרא tests whether משיכה acquires in a deal with a גוי. A ברייתא about buying scrap that contains an idol is explained by אביי and then רבא without disproving that view. Then a משנה about setting the price is used against רב אשי, and both sides end up explaining it by whether the buyer relied on the deal. Finally רבינא challenges רב אשי from the death penalty for a בן נח who steals. The answer is that he is punished for causing a Jew distress, not because his taking acquired the item.

steps.title: The buyer owns the wine before it becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רב: the גוי acquires the wine by pulling it, and only afterward does his touch make it יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the moment the gentile pulled it, he acquired it, and it did not become libation wine until he touched it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to רב's ruling. It points out that the order of events seems to favor the Jewish seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the גוי pulls the wine (משיכה), it legally belongs to him. Only after that does his touch make it יין נסך. So at the moment of sale the wine was still permitted, and the money he owes should be permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: a way of acquiring movable objects
Wine that is forbidden because a גוי may have used it for idol worship

phrases.english: From when the gentile pulled it, he acquired it,

phrases.aramaic: יֵין נֶסֶךְ לָא הָוֵי עַד דְּנָגַע בֵּיהּ!
phrases.english: but it does not become libation wine until he touches it!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that money from wine measured before payment is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acquisition by משיכה comes before the touch that makes the wine forbidden, so the sale involved permitted wine.

steps.title: רב means pouring into the buyer's own vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that pouring into a Jew's vessel would be fine, but says רב is talking about pouring into the גוי's vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he measures and pours into a Jew's vessel, that is indeed so. The ruling is needed only where he measures and pours into the gentile's vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by narrowing his case to wine poured into the גוי's own vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי's vessel already holds forbidden wine, so the poured wine becomes forbidden as soon as it touches what is in the vessel. That happens before the גוי ever pulls it. So in this case the wine is forbidden before he acquires it, and רב's ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּקָא כָיֵיל וְרָמֵי לְמָנָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: If he measures and pours into a Jew's vessel,
so it is indeed (permitted).
It is needed only where he measures
and pours into the gentile's vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּקָא כָיֵיל וְרָמֵי לְמָנָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by limiting רב's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב was talking about any sale where the גוי pulls the wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means wine poured into the גוי's vessel, where it becomes forbidden before משיכה.

steps.title: The vessel's airspace should acquire first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the גוי's vessel acquires the wine as soon as the wine enters its airspace. That happens before the wine reaches the bottom and becomes forbidden, unless רב holds ניצוק חיבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ultimately, when it reaches the vessel's airspace he acquires it, and it does not become libation wine until it reaches the bottom of the vessel. Shall we conclude that a stream is a connection?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 2. It asks whether רב's ruling would only work if a pouring stream connects the two liquids (ניצוק חיבור).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's vessel acquires for him, so the wine belongs to the גוי once it enters the vessel's airspace. It touches the forbidden wine only when it reaches the bottom. The only way the wine could be forbidden first is if the stream links the wine above to the forbidden wine below.

keyTerms.meaning: A poured stream connects the liquid above to the liquid below

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי מְטָא לְאַוֵּירָא דְּמָנָא קַנְיֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Ultimately, when it reaches the vessel's airspace, he acquires it,
yet it does not become libation wine
until it reaches the bottom of the vessel,
shall we learn from this that a stream is a connection?

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף כִּי מְטָא לְאַוֵּירָא דְּמָנָא קַנְיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב is talking about the גוי's vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vessel's airspace acquires the wine before it touches the forbidden wine. That would force רב to hold ניצוק חיבור.

steps.title: The vessel is resting on the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ניצוק חיבור is not needed. רב is talking about a vessel set on the ground, which does not acquire for the גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If the gentile holds the vessel in his hand, that is indeed so. The ruling is needed only where it is set on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that רב holds ניצוק חיבור. It narrows the case once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי holds the vessel, he acquires the wine in the airspace before it becomes forbidden, so the money is permitted. When the vessel rests on the ground, nothing acquires for him first. The wine becomes forbidden at the bottom before any acquisition, so רב's ruling stands without ניצוק חיבור.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא rejects the proof that רב holds ניצוק חיבור. The case of a vessel on the ground is challenged in the next step, and step 7 gives the final explanation of רב's case.

phrases.english: No. If the gentile is holding it,
the vessel, in his hand, so it is indeed (permitted);
it is needed only where it is set on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִי דְּנָקֵיט לֵיהּ גּוֹי לִכְלִי בִּידֵיהּ הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 and rejects the proof of ניצוק חיבור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring into any vessel of the גוי's would mean the wine is acquired in the airspace.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vessel on the ground does not acquire, so the wine is forbidden before acquisition, without ניצוק חיבור.

steps.title: Why doesn't the גוי's vessel acquire the wine for him?
steps.stepSummary: Even if the vessel sits on the ground, the גוי's own vessel should acquire the wine for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let his vessel acquire the wine for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from Step 4. It says that even a vessel resting on the ground is still the גוי's own vessel, so it should acquire the wine for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's own vessel can acquire things placed into it. If so, the wine would belong to the גוי the moment it enters his jug, before it becomes יין נסך. Then the Jew could take the money afterward, and רב's warning would not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: acquiring an item by having it placed into one's own vessel

phrases.english: But let his vessel acquire it for him!
phrases.notes: "His vessel" is the גוי's jug from Step 4, the one sitting on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 4, which said a vessel on the ground does not acquire.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 4 that a vessel on the ground does not acquire for the גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A buyer's own vessel acquires for him. So the wine is his before it becomes forbidden, and there is no problem taking money afterward.

steps.title: Proposed proof: a buyer's vessel in the seller's area does not acquire
steps.stepSummary: Since רב still forbids the money, it seems the buyer's vessel does not acquire while it is in the seller's area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn from this that when a buyer's vessel is in the seller's domain, the buyer does not acquire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to answer its own question: maybe רב holds that a buyer's vessel standing in the seller's area does not acquire for the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug is standing in the Jewish shopkeeper's store, which is the seller's area. If a vessel in the seller's area does not acquire, then the wine is not yet the גוי's when it becomes forbidden. This would make רב's ruling a proof for a disputed question about קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: in the domain or area of

phrases.english: Can you learn from this:
that the buyer's vessel in the seller's domain —
the buyer does not acquire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way out of Step 5's question by drawing a general rule from רב's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain does not acquire for the buyer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that one must take the money before pouring into the גוי's vessel.

steps.title: No proof: leftover wine on the rim forbids each drop right away
steps.stepSummary: The buyer's vessel really does acquire. רב is talking about a jug with leftover wine on its rim, which forbids each drop the moment it touches.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really I can tell you that the buyer does acquire. But what case are we dealing with here? A case where there is leftover wine on the mouth of the jug, so each drop, one after another, becomes יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 6. It explains רב's case in a different way, so no rule about the buyer's vessel can be learned from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that the buyer's vessel acquires. But in רב's case, the rim of the גוי's jug already has some of his wine on it. Each drop touches that wine at the very top and becomes forbidden before it ever enters the jug and is acquired.

keyTerms.meaning: really, I can tell you (the earlier idea still stands)
what case are we dealing with here?

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling does not prove that a buyer's vessel fails to acquire. It is about a jug whose rim already has wine on it, so the wine becomes forbidden at the rim.

phrases.english: No, really I can tell you:
the buyer does acquire,
but what case are we dealing with here?
Such as where there is leftover wine
on the mouth of the jug,
so each bit, one after another, becomes forbidden wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 6 and answers Step 5 by setting up a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain does not acquire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling can be explained by leftover wine on the rim, which forbids the wine before the vessel acquires it.

steps.title: This does not fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Under רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a mixture with יין נסך may be sold except for the value of the forbidden part, so the money should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose opinion is this? It is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. If it were like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he says: all of it may be sold to non-Jews, except for the value of the יין נסך in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 7. It says the answer seems to go against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, a small amount of forbidden wine on the rim mixes with a lot of permitted wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that such a mixture can be sold to non-Jews, as long as you do not take money for the forbidden part. By that view, the Jew could take money for nearly all the wine, so why does רב forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: and like whom? (whose opinion is this?)
wine forbidden because it may have been used for idol worship

phrases.english: And like whom?
It is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָאָמַר:
phrases.english: for if it were רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, doesn't he say:
all of it may be sold to non-Jews
except for the value of the יין נסך in it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְמַאן? דְּלָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case setup of Step 7 using רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on mixtures.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in Step 7 that leftover wine on the rim forbids all the poured wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a little forbidden wine mixed in does not forbid the money for the rest. So רב's warning would not fit his view.

steps.title: רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for barrels, not wine mixed with wine
steps.stepSummary: רב himself said he follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only when a barrel is mixed with barrels, not when wine is mixed into wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason anyone's but רב's? And רב said: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל when a barrel is mixed with barrels, but not when wine is mixed with wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 8. This ruling is רב's, and רב only follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in a narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב limits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's leniency to a forbidden barrel that got lost among permitted barrels. When forbidden wine actually mixes into permitted wine, as on the rim here, רב does not allow it. So Step 7's explanation stands, and nothing about the buyer's vessel can be proven from רב.

keyTerms.meaning: is the reason anything other than (it fits the speaker's own view)
a barrel mixed among other barrels

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for barrel among barrels. When wine is mixed into wine, it is all forbidden, so the explanation about the rim fits רב's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל completely. He follows him in the barrel case and only parts ways when wine is actually mixed into wine.

phrases.english: Is the reason anyone's but רב's?
phrases.notes: The ruling under discussion is רב's own, so we only need it to fit רב's view.

phrases.english: And didn't רב say:
the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל —
for a barrel mixed among barrels,
but not for wine mixed with wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by narrowing how far רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an authority's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in every mixture, so a small amount of forbidden wine should not forbid the money.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only for barrel among barrels. Wine mixed into wine is forbidden, so the explanation about the rim holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles that רב's ruling is consistent. The earlier attempt to prove a rule about a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain stays unproven.

steps.title: A challenge from the case of buying broken vessels that contain an idol
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if a Jew pulled the vessels before paying, he may return the idol to the גוי. If משיכה acquired for a גוי, the idol would already belong to the Jew, so why may he give it back?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A person bought scrap vessels from גוים and found an idol among them. If he pulled the items before paying, he may give the idol back. If he pulled them after paying, he must throw it into the Dead Sea. If pulling acquires with a גוי, why may he give it back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the view of אמימר that משיכה acquires in a deal with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If pulling made the Jew the owner, the idol would be a Jew's idol the moment he pulled it, and he would have to destroy it. Yet the ברייתא lets him return it as long as he had not paid. That suggests only paying מעות makes the purchase final with a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling an item, a way of acquiring it
The Dead Sea, where forbidden items are thrown so no one can use them

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who buys broken vessels from the gentiles
and found an idol among them,

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן מָעוֹת מָשַׁךְ — יַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: if he pulled before he gave money, he may return it,

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִשֶּׁנָּתַן מָעוֹת מָשַׁךְ — יוֹלִיךְ לְיָם הַמֶּלַח.
phrases.english: if he pulled after he gave money, he must take it to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: He must throw it away where no one can use it, since an idol may not be kept or benefited from.

phrases.english: If it enters your mind
that pulling acquires with a gentile,
why may he return it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the view that משיכה acquires for a גוי, after the previous discussion about רב's case was resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of אמימר that משיכה acquires in a deal with a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pulling acquired, the idol would belong to the Jew once pulled and could not be returned. The ברייתא allows returning it, so pulling must not acquire.

steps.title: אביי: he may return it because it looks like a mistaken purchase
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that pulling does acquire, but the Jew may return the idol because the deal looks like a מקח טעות. He never meant to buy an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because it looks like a mistaken purchase.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends אמימר by giving a different reason why the idol may be returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the Jew really did acquire the items by pulling them. Still, the idol can be returned because nobody wants to buy an idol, so this part of the deal counts as a mistake. The return is not because the deal never happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken purchase, which can be undone

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Because it looks like a mistaken transaction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מִשּׁוּם דְּמִיחֲזֵי כִּי מִקָּח טָעוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the ruling in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The return is allowed because pulling did not acquire.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pulling does acquire. The return is allowed because the deal is a מקח טעות.

steps.title: רבא: why is only the first case a mistaken purchase?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי. If buying an idol by mistake makes it a מקח טעות, that is just as true when he paid first. So why must he throw it away in the second case?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is the first case a mistaken purchase and the second case not a mistaken purchase?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from the second half of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistake is the same in both cases, since he never wanted an idol whether he paid first or pulled first. If מקח טעות were the reason to return it, he should be able to return it in the second case too. אביי's reason therefore cannot explain why the two halves differ.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a ברייתא or משנה
The last part of a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rava said:
The first clause is a mistaken transaction,
and the latter clause is not a mistaken transaction?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא רֵישָׁא מִקָּח טָעוּת סֵיפָא לָאו מִקָּח טָעוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the return is allowed because of מקח טעות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mistake is the same in both halves of the ברייתא, so מקח טעות cannot explain why only the first half allows returning the idol.

steps.title: רבא: both cases are mistakes, but only paying makes it look like a Jew owns an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that both cases are a מקח טעות. The difference is how things look. Before paying, people do not see the idol as being in a Jew's hands. After paying, it looks like a Jew owned an idol, so he must destroy it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Both the first and second case are mistaken purchases. In the first case, where he did not pay money, it does not look like an idol in a Jew's hands. In the second case, where he paid money, it looks like an idol in a Jew's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer for אמימר, explaining why the two halves of the ברייתא are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling still acquires, and both cases are a mistaken purchase. Once money is handed over, though, onlookers see an idol that a Jew bought and owned. So he must throw it into the ים המלח rather than give it back.

keyTerms.meaning: In the possession of a Jew

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of גרוטאות does not disprove אמימר. Pulling can acquire, and the difference between the cases is only about appearances once money was paid.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The first clause and the latter clause are both a mistaken transaction,
but in the first clause, where he did not pay money,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיתְחֲזֵי כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: it does not look like an idol in the possession of a Jew,
in the latter clause, where he paid money,
it looks like an idol in the possession of a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא מִקָּח טָעוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer after רבא's own challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the difference between the two cases by how things look to others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is that one case is a mistaken purchase and the other is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are mistaken purchases. Only after payment does it look like a Jew owns an idol.

steps.title: מר קשישא challenges רב אשי from the משנה about selling wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if a Jew set the price before measuring wine into a גוי's vessel, the money is permitted. If משיכה does not acquire for a גוי, the wine would still be the Jew's when it becomes יין נסך, so why is the money allowed?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא said to רב אשי: Come and hear: One who sells his wine to a גוי, if he set the price before he measured, the money is permitted. If you say pulling does not acquire with a גוי, why is the money permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the other side is attacked. מר קשישא uses the משנה to challenge רב אשי, who holds that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the wine into the גוי's vessel is the act of pulling. If that act acquires, the wine belongs to the גוי before it becomes forbidden, so the Jew's money is fine. If it does not acquire, the Jew still owns the wine when it becomes יין נסך, and the money he gets would be payment for forbidden wine.

keyTerms.meaning: He measured (poured the wine into the buyer's vessel)
Its money, the payment for it

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
One who sells his wine to a gentile,
if he fixed the price before he measured,
the money for it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מְשִׁיכָה בְּגוֹי אֵינָהּ קוֹנָה,
phrases.english: And if you say pulling does not acquire with a gentile,
why is the money for it permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Switches sides and now challenges רב אשי's view that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pulling does not acquire, the wine is still the Jew's when it becomes forbidden, so the money should be forbidden. The משנה permits it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the גוי paid a דינר in advance
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the גוי paid a דינר ahead of time. The money acquired the wine before it became forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he paid him a דינר in advance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends his view by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי agrees that money acquires for a גוי. If the גוי paid before the measuring, the wine was already his before he touched it. So the משנה does not prove that pulling acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with what case?
Where he paid him a dinar in advance.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן דְּאַקְדֵּים לֵיהּ דִּינָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is talking about a normal sale, so pulling must be what acquires.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a case where money was paid first, and the money is what acquired.

steps.title: Challenge from the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about a case where a דינר was paid first, the second half does not fit. There, measuring before setting the price makes the money forbidden. If a דינר was already paid, why should it be forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say the last part: If he measured before he set the price, the money is forbidden. If he paid him a דינר in advance, why is the money forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer by reading the next part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half most likely refers to the same kind of case. If the גוי had already paid a דינר, the money should have acquired the wine before it became forbidden, even without a set price. Yet the משנה forbids the money, so the 'paid in advance' answer seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (read the next clause)

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
If he measured before he fixed the price,
the money for it is forbidden,
but if he paid him a dinar in advance,
why is the money for it forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the משנה is talking about a case where a דינר was paid in advance
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a דינר was paid in advance, the money should acquire in the second half too, yet that half forbids the money.

steps.title: רב אשי turns the question back on the challenger
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the challenger's question with a question of his own. Even in the challenger's view, that משיכה acquires for a גוי, the רישא and סיפא of the משנה give different rulings. So the challenger also has to explain that difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And according to you, who say that משיכה acquires for a גוי, why is the money permitted in the first case and forbidden in the second?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי does not answer the challenger directly. Instead he points out that the challenger, who holds that משיכה acquires for a גוי, has the very same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenger asked why the money is forbidden in the סיפא if a דינר was already paid. רב אשי replies that even if pulling acquires, the wine was pulled in both halves of the משנה. Yet the משנה still gives different rulings. So the challenger must also explain the difference, and whatever he says will work for רב אשי too.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to you (your own view)
Pulling an item toward oneself, a way of acquiring it
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
Its money (the payment for the wine)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not a final attack. It is a 'you have the same problem' reply. רב אשי is setting up the point that one answer will solve the difficulty for both sides.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering the one who challenged him from the משנה.

phrases.english: And according to you, who say
that pulling acquires in a deal with a gentile,
why in the first clause is its money permitted,
and in the last clause is its money forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-question in response to the challenge of Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The challenger's (מר קשישא's side) view that משיכה acquires for a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the challenger's view the wine was pulled in both cases, so it was acquired in both. Yet the משנה rules differently in the two cases, so the challenger faces the same difficulty.

steps.title: The challenger's own answer: setting the price creates reliance
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says what the challenger must answer. When a price was set, the buyer relies on the deal, so the acquisition works. When no price was set, he does not rely on it, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? When he set the price, the buyer relies on the deal. When he did not set the price, the buyer does not rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out the answer the challenger would have to give. This sets up the next step, where רב אשי uses the same answer for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between the two halves of the משנה is not about how the wine was acquired. It is about whether the buyer was settled in his mind (סמכא דעתיה). Without a set price, the deal is not firm, so the purchase never takes hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what do you have to say? (what answer will you give)
His mind relies on it; he is confident the deal is final

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
If he set the price, his mind relies on the deal;
if he did not set the price, his mind does not rely on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the answer the challenger would give to the counter-question of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the buyer's reliance (whether a price was set)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the משנה seem to differ only in how the wine was acquired.
steps.terutzMaskana: The halves differ because setting a price makes the buyer rely on the deal, and that reliance is what lets the acquisition work.

steps.title: רב אשי uses the same answer for his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the same answer works for him. Even when a דינר was paid in advance, the acquisition only works if a price was set and the buyer relied on the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to me too: even though the buyer gave him a דינר in advance, if he set the price the buyer relies on the deal, and if he did not set the price the buyer does not rely on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the challenger's answer and applies it to his own case of a דינר paid in advance. This fully answers the question from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying a דינר ahead of time can acquire the wine, but only if the buyer truly relies on the deal. In the סיפא no price was set yet. So even the דינר did not lock in the purchase before the wine became forbidden, and the money is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the key point. Whether money or pulling acquires, the purchase only takes hold when a price was set, so that the buyer relies on the deal. That is why the רישא and סיפא of the משנה differ.

phrases.english: According to me as well,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּקְדֵים לֵיהּ דִּינָר —
phrases.english: even though he gave him a dinar in advance,
if he set the price, his mind relies on the deal;
if he did not set the price, his mind does not rely on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer from Step 18 to רב אשי's own reading from Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same distinction applied to both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A דינר paid in advance should always acquire the wine, so the money in the סיפא should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The דינר acquires only if a price was set. In the סיפא no price was set, so the purchase did not take hold in time.

steps.title: New challenge: a בן נח is killed for stealing less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a new challenge against רב אשי from רבי יוחנן. A בן נח is killed even for stealing less than a פרוטה. If משיכה does not acquire for a גוי, his taking of the item should not count, so why is he killed?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a בן נח is killed for stealing less than a פרוטה, even though he does not have to give it back. If you say משיכה does not acquire for a גוי, why is he killed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new attack on רב אשי's view, using a teaching of רבי יוחנן about a בן נח who steals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stealing means taking the item into your own control. If a גוי cannot acquire by משיכה, then grabbing an item does nothing legally, because it stays the owner's. Yet רבי יוחנן says he is killed, which suggests his pulling does count.

keyTerms.meaning: A descendant of נח, meaning a non-Jew
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest amount of money that counts
Must be returned (given back as payment)

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the debate from buying wine to the laws of theft. The question becomes whether a גוי's act of taking has legal power at all.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear,
as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A descendant of Noah is executed
for stealing less than the value of a peruta,
and it is not subject to being returned,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מְשִׁיכָה בְּגוֹי אֵינָהּ קוֹנָה,
phrases.english: and if you say that pulling does not acquire for a gentile,
why is he executed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה-based debate is settled, רבינא brings a new source against רב אשי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's view that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בן נח is killed for stealing. Stealing requires taking the item into one's possession. If משיכה does not work for a גוי, he never took it legally, so there should be no death penalty.

steps.title: He is killed for causing a Jew distress
steps.stepSummary: The answer to רבינא's challenge: a בן נח is put to death for stealing because he caused pain to a Jew. That does not depend on whether his taking legally acquired the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he caused distress to a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא's question from step 20. The בן נח is killed because he hurt a Jew by taking his item, not because he legally acquired it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed the death penalty only makes sense if the גוי's grabbing counts as a real acquisition. The answer separates the two ideas: the punishment comes from the harm done to the owner, not from a legal transfer of ownership. So רב אשי can keep his view that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: He caused him pain or distress

steps.whatToRemember: A בן נח's punishment for stealing is based on the distress he causes the owner. It does not prove that his taking counts as a legal קנין, so רב אשי's position stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer means the גוי acquired the item. The point is the opposite: he can be punished even though, by the rules of קנין, he did not acquire it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a punishment for stealing and the legal rules of acquisition are two separate questions. One does not prove the other.

phrases.english: Because he caused distress to a Jew.
phrases.notes: "He" is the בן נח who stole from step 20. Taking the item hurt the Jewish owner, even though no real קנין happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבינא's challenge from רבי יוחנן's teaching in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the law: the death penalty comes from the harm done, not from a legal acquisition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא thought the בן נח could only be killed if his grabbing (משיכה) legally acquired the item for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death penalty is based on causing a Jew distress. So it fits even if משיכה does not acquire for a גוי, and רב אשי's view stands.
